mainTopic: The evening קריאת שמע: the חצות fence, joining גאולה to תפילה at night, אשרי, and the bedtime שמע
overview: The גמרא asks why the חכמים set the deadline for evening קריאת שמע at חצות if they agree with רבן גמליאל that the Torah allows the whole night. It answers that חצות is only a protective fence. A ברייתא describes a tired worker who plans to rest first, falls asleep and misses שמע, and it warns that one who breaks the חכמים's words is חייב מיתה. The גמרא gives two reasons for that harsh warning: the real danger of falling asleep, or to teach that תפילת ערבית is a חובה. The same ברייתא then supports רבי יוחנן, who joins גאולה to the evening תפילה, against רבי יהושע בן לוי, who places the תפילות between the two readings of שמע. Their argument is explained through סברא and through the פסוק ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״. The גמרא also shows that הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ does not break the link between גאולה and תפילה. Several אגדות follow: why תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד is special, why אשרי has no נ verse, and how fast different angels fly. The amud ends with רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule to say שמע again on one's bed, and רב נחמן begins a comment that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the Sages agree with רבן גמליאל, why don't they rule like him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: if they read 'ובשכבך' as the whole night like רבן גמליאל, their ruling should match his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the חכמים hold like רבן גמליאל, then they should rule like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a mismatch. If the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל about what the פסוק means, why does their deadline differ from his?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל says evening קריאת שמע can be said until dawn, because 'when you lie down' covers the whole night. If the חכמים understand the פסוק the same way, their 'until חצות' seems to have no source. The challenge is: either disagree with the reading, or match the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who says evening קריאת שמע may be said until dawn
They hold / that is their opinion

phrases.english: And if they hold like Rabban Gamliel —
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים.

phrases.english: let them say like Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about how the חכמים read 'ובשכבך'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the source covers the whole night, a midnight deadline looks inconsistent with that source.

steps.title: The Sages agree, but midnight is a protective deadline
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים really do hold like רבן גמליאל. They set חצות only to keep people away from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they do hold like רבן גמליאל. When they say 'until חצות,' it is to keep a person far from transgression.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The חכמים fully agree that the Torah allows the whole night, but they set an earlier deadline as a safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two levels: what the Torah allows (all night) and what the חכמים require (by חצות). The midnight deadline is a fence, not a different reading of the פסוק. This removes the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to keep the original position while explaining it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים disagree with רבן גמליאל about the Torah law. They agree it is the whole night. 'Until חצות' is only their protective rule on top of that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the halacha: we try to say evening קריאת שמע before חצות, but the Torah obligation itself lasts until dawn.

phrases.english: Really, they hold like Rabban Gamliel,
and the fact that they say "until midnight"

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְהַרְחִיק אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעֲבֵירָה.
phrases.english: is in order to distance a person from transgression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the ruling as a rabbinic safeguard rather than a different reading of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'until חצות' meant the חכמים read the פסוק differently from רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: They read it the same way. חצות is only a protective fence.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the fence and the tired worker
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that the חכמים made a fence, so that a tired worker won't delay and fall asleep for the whole night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the חכמים made a fence for their words. Otherwise a person might come home from the field in the evening and say, 'I'll go home, eat a little, drink a little, sleep a little, and then say קריאת שמע and pray.' Then sleep grabs him and he sleeps the whole night. Instead, a person coming from the field in the evening goes into the בית הכנסת. If he usually reads Torah, he reads. If he usually learns משנה, he learns. Then he says קריאת שמע and prays, and afterward eats his meal and says the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the idea that the midnight deadline is a fence. It paints a real-life picture of how someone can miss קריאת שמע, and shows the right way to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states outright that the חכמים made a סייג, which proves the answer in step 2. The danger is the 'just a little' plan: eat, drink, nap, then pray. The fix is to say קריאת שמע and pray first, before eating at home.

keyTerms.meaning: Sleep grabs him, he gets overcome by sleep

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of davening מעריב before sitting down to a meal at night.

phrases.english: As it was taught: the Sages made a fence for their words,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה בָּעֶרֶב,
phrases.english: so that a person should not come from the field in the evening,
and say: "I will go home and eat a little,
and drink a little, and sleep a little,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֶקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְאֶתְפַּלֵּל״,
phrases.english: and afterward I will recite Shema and pray,"

phrases.aramaic: וְחוֹטַפְתּוֹ שֵׁינָה וְנִמְצָא יָשֵׁן כָּל הַלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: and sleep overtakes him and he ends up sleeping the whole night.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה בָּעֶרֶב,
phrases.english: Rather, a person comes from the field in the evening,
goes into the synagogue,
if he is used to reading Scripture, he reads.
And if he is used to learning Mishnah, he learns,
and he recites Shema and prays,
and eats his bread and says the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the חצות deadline is a rabbinic fence
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'חכמים עשו סייג לדבריהם' with the example of the tired worker

steps.title: The ברייתא's harsh warning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that anyone who breaks the words of the חכמים is חייב מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who goes against the words of the חכמים deserves death.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא, a very strong warning. It sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא backs up the fence with the harshest possible language. Saying such a thing about a rabbinic rule is surprising, and the גמרא is about to ask about it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that 'until חצות' is a סייג of the חכמים, and it ends with a strong warning: חייב מיתה.

phrases.english: And anyone who transgresses the words of the Sages
is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָל הָעוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים חַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The closing line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who violates the words of the חכמים is חייב מיתה.

steps.title: Why does this rule get a death warning when others don't?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says 'חייב מיתה' here, when it says nothing like that about other rabbinic rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about all other places, where it does not teach 'חייב מיתה,' and what is different here, where it does teach 'חייב מיתה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the harsh warning. It asks what makes this rule special, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are many rabbinic fences, and normally no death warning is attached. So the גמרא looks for something unique about the קריאת שמע fence that would explain the extra strong language.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (in the ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: What is different in all other places
that it does not teach "liable to death,"
and what is different here
that it teaches "liable to death"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּכָל דּוּכְתָּא דְּלָא קָתָנֵי חַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the unusual wording at the end of the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why this particular rabbinic fence is backed by a 'חייב מיתה' warning when other rabbinic rules are not

steps.title: First answer: the danger of falling asleep
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses strong words here because a tired person can easily be overcome by sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because there is the danger of being overcome by sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question of why the ברייתא said 'חייב מיתה' only here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is not stricter than other rabbinic rules. The danger is that a tired worker will fall asleep and miss קריאת שמע completely. Because that danger is so real, the חכמים had to warn very strongly.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one possible answer
Being overcome by sleep without meaning to

phrases.english: If you want, say
it is because there is the danger of being overcome by sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא אוֹנֶס שֵׁינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strong warning is needed because the risk of falling asleep and missing שמע entirely is very high.

steps.title: Second answer: evening prayer is mandatory
steps.stepSummary: The strong words teach against the view that תפילת ערבית is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: it comes to reject the one who says 'the evening prayer is optional.' It teaches us that it is mandatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer for the strong words 'חייב מיתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some held that תפילת ערבית is only רשות. The ברייתא speaks so strongly to make clear that it is a חובה. So the warning is about the evening davening, not only about שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude or reject another opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for 'חייב מיתה': the danger of falling asleep, or to teach that תפילת ערבית is a חובה.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
it comes to reject the one who says
'The evening prayer is optional.'
It teaches us that it is mandatory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strong language rejects the view that תפילת ערבית is רשות and teaches that it is a חובה.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says to read שמע and then daven at night, which supports רבי יוחנן's teaching about joining גאולה to the evening תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: he reads קריאת שמע and prays. This supports רבי יוחנן. For רבי יוחנן said: Who is destined for the World to Come? One who joins the blessing of redemption to the evening prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a detail in the ברייתא and shows that it backs up a teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the worker says שמע first and only then davens. רבי יוחנן says that at night you should go straight from the ברכה of גאולה, which comes after שמע, into שמונה עשרה. Since the ברייתא puts שמע right before תפילה, it fits רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: quotes a line from the source just learned
One destined for the World to Come
One who joins the redemption blessing directly to שמונה עשרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for going straight from גאל ישראל into שמונה עשרה at מעריב as well.

phrases.english: The Master said,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא from step 3 about the worker coming home from the field.

phrases.english: he reads קריאת שמע and prays.
This supports רבי יוחנן.
For רבי יוחנן said:
Who is destined for the World to Come?
It is one who joins redemption
phrases.notes: "Redemption" means the ברכה right after שמע that speaks of how הקב"ה redeemed us.

phrases.english: to the evening prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמִתְפַּלֵּל מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חייב מיתה question and uses another line of the same ברייתא for a new point.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that at night one should join גאולה to תפילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording 'reads קריאת שמע and prays', putting שמע right before תפילה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the prayers go in the middle
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that the day's תפילות were set between the morning שמע and the evening שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: The prayers were established in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opposing opinion to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע בן לוי, the two readings of שמע are like bookends: morning שמע at the start, evening שמע at the end, and all the תפילות in between. So at night he davens ערבית first and says שמע after it, which is the opposite of רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Both agree that in the morning שמע comes before שמונה עשרה. They argue only about the night.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן לוי says:
The prayers were established in the middle.
phrases.notes: "In the middle" means between the morning שמע and the evening שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אוֹמֵר תְּפִלּוֹת בָּאֶמְצַע תִּקְּנוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that disagrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the תפילות are placed between the morning and evening שמע, so at night תפילה comes before שמע.

steps.title: What is their argument based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the root of the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind each side. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know what each one does in practice. Now the גמרא wants the source or reasoning that leads each side to his view.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? Asks for the root of a מחלוקת

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the מחלוקת just presented.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying source or reasoning of the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Either a verse or reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument can be explained either from a פסוק or from סברא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is a verse; if you want, say it is logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two ways to explain the מחלוקת. This is a setup line, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is announcing two possible roots: one based on reading a פסוק, the other based on reasoning. Each will be explained in the coming lines.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is a verse;
if you want, say it is logic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute can be traced either to a פסוק or to a סברא, with the details still to come.

steps.title: The logic approach: רבי יוחנן's view of the night redemption
steps.stepSummary: Using סברא, the גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן holds the redemption from מצרים already began at night, even though it was only complete in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the argument is about logic. רבי יוחנן holds that the redemption started at night too, but the full redemption only came in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the first explanation, the סברא way. It tells us how רבי יוחנן thinks about the redemption from מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The redemption from מצרים had two parts: something happened at night, and the full going-out happened in the morning. רבי יוחנן says the night part still counts as גאולה. So at night it also makes sense to join the גאולה ברכה to the תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic or reasoning, as opposed to learning from a פסוק
Redemption; here the redemption from מצרים, which the ברכה after שמע talks about
Full, complete, of the best kind

phrases.english: If you want, say it is a matter of logic.
For רבי יוחנן holds:
there was redemption from the evening too,
but the full redemption
did not happen until the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the סברא option that step 11 mentioned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוחנן, the night already had some redemption, so night גאולה is real enough to join to תפילה.

steps.title: The logic approach: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that since the redemption only really happened in the morning, the night had no full redemption, so there is no need to join גאולה to the night תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds: since the redemption only happened from the morning, at night it was not a full redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the סברא explanation. רבי יהושע בן לוי looks at the same facts and comes out the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rabbis agree on the history: the complete redemption was in the morning. The only argument is whether the partial night redemption counts. רבי יהושע בן לוי says it does not, so night has no real גאולה to join to the תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the סברא approach, both agree that the full redemption was in the morning. They only argue whether the partial night redemption is enough to join גאולה to the night תפילה.

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע בן לוי holds:
since it only happened from the morning,
there was no full redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סָבַר כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוְיָא אֶלָּא מִצַּפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the same סברא explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, night redemption is not full, so it is not joined to תפילה.

steps.title: The verse approach: both learn from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second explanation: both rabbis learn their view from the same words, ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say the argument comes from a פסוק. Both of them learned from the same פסוק, as it says: 'when you lie down and when you rise.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the second explanation, the פסוק way. This line sets up the next two steps, where each rabbi reads the פסוק his own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is not about history or logic. Both rabbis use the same words of the תורה but read them differently. The next steps show how.

keyTerms.meaning: They explained or learned from (a פסוק)
When you lie down and when you rise, from the פרשה of שמע

phrases.english: And if you want, say it comes from a verse,
and both of them learned from one verse,
as it is written: 'When you lie down and when you rise.'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the סברא explanation and opens the פסוק explanation mentioned in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument comes from different readings of ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן compares the order of night to morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as comparing lying down to rising. Just as in the morning שמע comes and then תפילה, so at night it is שמע and then תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds: the פסוק compares lying down to getting up. Just as when getting up it is שמע and then תפילה, so too when lying down it is שמע and then תפילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק. Night should follow the same order as morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning everyone agrees that we say שמע and its ברכות and then go straight into תפילה. רבי יוחנן says the פסוק puts night and morning together, so night copies that order. That is why at night too we join גאולה to תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares; puts two things side by side so one learns from the other

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן holds:
the verse compares lying down to rising.
Just as with rising,
it is the reading of שמע and after that תפילה,
so too with lying down,
it is the reading of שמע and after that תפילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: מַקִּישׁ שְׁכִיבָה לְקִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק introduced in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison is about order: night, like morning, is שמע followed by תפילה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי compares the timing of night to morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי uses the same comparison but says it is about timing. Just as morning שמע is said right when you get out of bed, night שמע is said right when you go to bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds: the פסוק compares lying down to getting up. Just as when getting up, שמע is close to his bed, so too when lying down, שמע is close to his bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of the same פסוק. For him the comparison is about when you say שמע, not about what comes after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rabbis agree the פסוק compares night to morning. רבי יוחנן learns the order, שמע then תפילה. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns the timing: night שמע should be said close to going to sleep, so it cannot be tied to the evening תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to explain the מחלוקת: (1) סברא: does the partial night redemption from מצרים count as גאולה? (2) פסוק: ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ compares night to morning. רבי יוחנן says it compares the order (שמע then תפילה). רבי יהושע בן לוי says it compares the timing (שמע close to bed).
steps.confusionAlert: Both rabbis use the exact same comparison, מַקִּישׁ שְׁכִיבָה לְקִימָה. They do not argue about whether the comparison exists. They argue about what it compares.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds:
the verse compares lying down to rising.
Just as with rising,
the reading of שמע is close to his bed,
phrases.notes: In the morning, 'when you rise' means right when you get out of bed.

phrases.english: so too with lying down,
the reading of שמע is close to his bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סָבַר: מַקִּישׁ שְׁכִיבָה לְקִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק and finishes the פסוק explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison is about timing: night שמע, like morning שמע, is said close to the bed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one פסוק and one comparison can support two opposite practices, depending on what the comparison is understood to focus on.

steps.title: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ seems to break the link at night
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא asks how רבי יוחנן's rule can work at night, since הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ is said between גאולה and תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא objected: A משנה says that at night you say two ברכות before שמע and two after it. If you say you must join גאולה to תפילה, you are not joining them, because you still have to say הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ in between!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view that at night you must go straight from גאולה into תפילה. A משנה shows there is another ברכה, הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ, said in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברכות after שמע at night are גאל ישראל and הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ. Since הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ comes after the גאולה ברכה, it seems to sit between גאולה and תפילה and break the link. So how can רבי יוחנן require joining them at night?

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (usually from an earlier source)
To join, to place right next to
Redemption; the ברכה about leaving מצרים
"Let us lie down"; the second ברכה after שמע at night

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, raises an objection:
In the evening one recites
two blessings before it and two after it.
And if you say one must join them,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא קָא סָמֵךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה,
phrases.english: look, he is not joining redemption to prayer,
since he must say "Help us lie down"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's view that at night שמע (with גאולה) must come right before תפילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule of joining גאולה to תפילה at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ after the גאולה ברכה, which seems to interrupt between גאולה and תפילה.

steps.title: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ counts as part of the גאולה blessing
steps.stepSummary: Because the Rabbis set up הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ, it is treated as an extension of the גאולה ברכה, not a break.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Since the Rabbis set up הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ, it is like one long גאולה ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ does not interrupt, because it counts as part of the גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A break only counts as a break if it is something separate. Since the Rabbis themselves placed הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ there, it becomes part of the גאולה section. So גאולה still flows right into תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like, it is considered

phrases.english: They say:
Since the Rabbis instituted "Help us lie down,"
it is like one long redemption blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the supposed interruption as part of the original unit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ is a separate ברכה that breaks the link between גאולה and תפילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Rabbis set it there, הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ is part of an extended גאולה, so no break exists.

steps.title: Proof from the morning: the same problem exists there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows we must accept this idea, because otherwise even in the morning ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ would break the link.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say this, how could anyone join גאולה to תפילה in the morning? רבי יוחנן said that at the start of תפילה you say ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״, and at the end you say ״יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer by pointing to the morning. There is also something said between גאולה and תפילה in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן himself says to start תפילה with ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״. That פסוק comes after גאולה, so it too seems like a break. Since no one thinks the morning link is broken, an added piece set up by the Rabbis must not count as a break.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so
"Lord, open my lips"; said before שמונה עשרה
"May they be accepted"; said at the end of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
how can one join them in the morning?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
At the beginning one says: "Lord, open my lips,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:17

phrases.english: and at the end he says:
"May the words of my mouth be acceptable."
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:15

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, שַׁחֲרִית הֵיכִי מָצֵי סָמֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 18 by showing the same issue in the morning.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a passage the Rabbis set up is not an interruption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ is said before the morning תפילה.

steps.title: Both added pieces are part of the main unit
steps.stepSummary: Just as ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ counts as part of a long תפילה, הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ counts as part of a long גאולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, in the morning, since the Rabbis set up ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״, it is like one long תפילה. Here too, since the Rabbis set up הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ, it is like one long גאולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It explains the morning case and then applies the same rule to the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning, the added פסוק is attached to the תפילה that comes after it. At night, הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ is attached to the גאולה that comes before it. Either way, nothing separate stands between גאולה and תפילה, so רבי יוחנן's view holds.
steps.whatToRemember: Something the Rabbis set up between גאולה and תפילה does not break the link. In the morning ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ is part of תפילה, and at night הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ is part of גאולה.
steps.confusionAlert: The two added pieces attach in opposite directions. ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ joins the תפילה after it, while הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ joins the גאולה before it.

phrases.english: Rather, there,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״
phrases.english: since the Rabbis instituted saying "Lord, open my lips,"
it is like one long prayer.
Here too,
since the Rabbis instituted saying "Help us lie down,"
it is like one long redemption blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof of step 19 and closes the challenge of step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Passages set up by the Rabbis count as part of the nearby section, so רבי יוחנן's joining of גאולה to תפילה works both morning and night.

steps.title: Saying תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד three times a day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אבינא teaches that whoever says תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד three times every day is promised עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אבינא: Anyone who says תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד three times every day is promised a share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching. It is about a daily practice that earns a promise of עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement, not part of the argument about גאולה and תפילה. It is placed here because רבי יוחנן also promised עולם הבא to someone who joins גאולה to תפילה. The גמרא will next explain why this specific מזמור gets this promise.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has a share in the World to Come

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Avina said:
Anyone who says "A praise of David"
phrases.notes: תהלים 145

phrases.english: three times every day

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: is promised that he has a share in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching placed here because, like רבי יוחנן's teaching about joining גאולה to תפילה, it promises עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד three times daily guarantees a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What makes תהלה לדוד so special?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אבינא's big promise about תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this one chapter of תהלים earns such a huge reward. This short question sets up a search for the reason, which comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise of עולם הבא in step 21 is very large, so the גמרא wants to know what quality of this chapter earns it. The answer has to be something this chapter has that other chapters do not.

keyTerms.meaning: תהלים פרק קמ״ה, the main part of what we call אשרי

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד in particular earns the promise of עולם הבא from step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the מימרא of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אבינא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which feature of תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד makes it worth the promise of עולם הבא.

steps.title: The alphabet reason is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is the אלף-בית order, then rejects it, because אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ has that order eight times over.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it goes in the order of the אלף-בית, then let a person say ״אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ״, which goes through the אלף-בית eight times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer: the chapter goes in the order of the אלף-בית. It knocks that answer down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אלף-בית order were the reason, then תהלים פרק קי״ט should be even better, since it has eight verses for each letter. Since nobody gives that chapter this promise, the alphabet alone cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Alphabetical order, with each verse starting with the next letter
The opening of תהלים פרק קי״ט

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ (פרק קי״ט) with the אשרי we say in davening (״אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ״ followed by תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד). They are different chapters.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it goes in alphabetical order,
then let him say ״Happy are they who are upright in the way״,
phrases.notes: תהלים 119

phrases.english: which goes through the alphabet eight times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 22 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the alphabet order as the whole reason for the promise.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another chapter, פרק קי״ט, has the alphabet order even more strongly, so this reason does not explain why תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד was chosen.

steps.title: The feeding reason is not enough either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is the verse ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״, then rejects it, because הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל also praises ה׳ for giving food to all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it contains ״You open Your hand״. Then let a person say הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל, where it is written ״Who gives bread to all flesh״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer: the chapter praises ה׳ for feeding every living thing. It knocks this answer down too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If praising ה׳ as the One who feeds the world were the reason, then הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל (תהלים קל״ו) should be just as good, since it says ״נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר״. So this feature alone is not unique to תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד either.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (it drops the last idea and tries a new one)
You open Your hand, the verse praising ה׳ for feeding every living thing
The Great Hallel, תהלים פרק קל״ו
Who gives bread to all flesh

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it contains
״You open Your hand״,
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:16

phrases.english: then let him say the Great Hallel,
phrases.notes: תהלים 136

phrases.english: in which it is written ״Who gives bread to all flesh״.
phrases.notes: תהלים 136:25

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the alphabet reason fails, a second reason is offered and also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects praise for feeding the world as the whole reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל also has this praise, so it does not explain why only תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד gets the promise.

steps.title: It has both features together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד is special because it has both the אלף-בית order and the praise of ה׳ feeding all creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it has both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the chapter is special because it has both qualities at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each feature alone is found elsewhere, which is why both earlier answers failed. But only תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד has the alphabet order and ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״ together, so the two rejected reasons combine into the real one.

keyTerms.meaning: Two things, here meaning both features together

steps.whatToRemember: תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד earns its promise of עולם הבא because it is the one chapter that has both the אלף-בית order and the praise ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why אשרי is so central in daily davening. It also shows a common move in the גמרא: two reasons that fail alone can succeed together.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it has both.
phrases.notes: Both means the alphabet order from step 23 and the feeding verse from step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two rejected reasons from steps 23 and 24 into the final answer to step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The special quality of תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד is that it has both features, the אלף-בית order and the praise of ה׳ as the One who feeds every living thing.

steps.title: Why there is no verse starting with נ in אשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אשרי has no נ verse because a well-known נ verse speaks about the downfall of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why is there no verse starting with נ in אשרי? Because the נ brings to mind the fall of 'the enemies of Israel,' as it says: 'Fallen, she will rise no more, the maiden of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching about אשרי. רבי יוחנן explains why one letter of the אלף-בית is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the אלף-בית order is part of what makes אשרי special, but the order skips נ. רבי יוחנן says this is on purpose. The verse in עמוס that begins with נ (נָפְלָה) describes Israel falling, so דוד did not want a נ verse in his praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'enemies of Israel,' a polite way of saying Israel itself
The 'maiden of Israel,' a poetic name for the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: ״שׂוֹנְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ here does not mean Israel's real enemies. It is a polite way to avoid saying something bad about Israel directly. The verse is talking about Israel falling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר נוּן בְּ״אַשְׁרֵי״ —
phrases.english: Why is there no נ said in Ashrei?
Because there is in it
the downfall of the enemies of Israel,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying the downfall of Israel itself.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'She has fallen, she will rise no more,
the maiden of Israel.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 5:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר נוּן בְּ״אַשְׁרֵי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the point that אשרי follows the אלף-בית by explaining why one letter is missing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשרי leaves out a נ verse because the נ verse in עמוס describes Israel's downfall.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they read the verse with hope
steps.stepSummary: In the West they read the עמוס verse differently: Israel fell but will not fall again, so rise up.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they explained it this way: 'She has fallen, and she will not fall again. Rise up, maiden of Israel!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way of reading the same sad verse. In ארץ ישראל they read it as a promise of hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By splitting the verse differently, 'she will no more' goes with falling instead of with rising. So 'rise' becomes a command: 'Rise, maiden of Israel!' The verse now promises that Israel will never fall again.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
They explain it, they read it

phrases.english: In the West they explain it like this:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: 'She has fallen, and she will not fall again;
rise, maiden of Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a hopeful reading of the same verse רבי יוחנן quoted, softening its harsh meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse can be read as: Israel fell once but will not fall again, so rise up.

steps.title: דוד gave support right away in the ס verse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that even though דוד left out the נ verse, he used רוח הקודש to support the fallen in the very next verse, ״סומך ה׳ לכל הנופלים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even so, דוד went back and supported them through רוח הקודש, as it says: 'ה׳ supports all who fall.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a comforting point to רבי יוחנן's teaching. The ס verse, right where the נ verse would have come, already answers the fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד skipped the letter of 'falling,' but he did not just leave Israel fallen. Through רוח הקודש he saw the later verse in עמוס, and in the next letter, ס, he wrote that ה׳ holds up all who fall. So the fall is answered right away with support.

keyTerms.meaning: He supported them, held them up

steps.whatToRemember: אשרי has no נ verse because נ brings to mind Israel's fall (נָפְלָה). But the very next verse, ס, says ״סומך ה׳ לכל הנופלים״: ה׳ holds up all who fall.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even what is left out of אשרי carries a message: the fall is not mentioned, but the support is.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Even so, David went back
and supported them through divine inspiration,
as it is said: 'The Lord supports all who fall.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:14. This is the ס verse, which comes right where the נ verse would have been.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, חָזַר דָּוִד וּסְמָכָן בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי יוחנן's explanation: the fall was left out, but support was put in right after.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through רוח הקודש, דוד followed the missing נ with the ס verse that ה׳ supports all who fall.

steps.title: מיכאל is described as faster than גבריאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא says the פסוקים describe מיכאל in a greater way than גבריאל: מיכאל arrives in one flight, while גבריאל needs two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא said: What is said about מיכאל is greater than what is said about גבריאל. About מיכאל it says, 'One of the שרפים flew to me,' but about גבריאל it says, 'The man גבריאל, whom I saw in the vision at first, flying, flying...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from the same רבי אלעזר, about two angels. He compares how the פסוקים describe their flying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מיכאל the verse uses one flying word, ״וַיָּעׇף״, so he got there in one flight. By גבריאל the verse doubles the word, ״מֻעָף בִּיעָף״, which shows it took him two flights. So מיכאל is described as greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Flying swiftly, literally 'made to fly in flight' (a double expression)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Avina said:
Greater is what is said about Michael
than what is said about Gabriel,
for about Michael it is written:
'And one of the seraphim flew to me.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 6:6. Just one word for flying, so one flight.

phrases.english: while regarding Gabriel it is written:
'And the man Gabriel, whom I had seen
in the vision at the beginning,
being made to fly swiftly, etc.'
phrases.notes: דניאל 9:21. The flying word is doubled, which shows two flights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר אֲבִינָא: גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמִיכָאֵל יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּגַבְרִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It is brought here because it is another teaching of the same רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיכאל reaches his mission in one flight, and גבריאל in two, so מיכאל is described as greater.

steps.title: How do we know the angel in ישעיהו is מיכאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the 'one' of the שרפים in ישעיהו is מיכאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this 'one' is מיכאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks a hidden assumption in רבי אלעזר's teaching. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא will bring a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ישעיהו only says 'one of the שרפים' and never gives a name. רבי אלעזר's whole comparison depends on that angel being מיכאל, so the גמרא asks for proof.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? How do we know?
'One,' the word in the verse being explained

phrases.english: From where is it implied that this 'one' is Michael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption in step 29 that the unnamed angel in ישעיהו is מיכאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the 'one' of the שרפים in ישעיהו 6:6 is מיכאל.

steps.title: The word 'one' links the שרף to מיכאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'אחד' to prove that the 'one' שרף in ישעיהו is מיכאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We learn it from the word 'one' in two places. Here it says 'And one of the שרפים flew to me,' and there it says 'And behold, מיכאל, one of the first chief ministers, came to help me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 30. It shows that the 'one' שרף in ישעיהו is מיכאל, because דניאל uses the same word 'one' for מיכאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו the angel is only called 'one of the שרפים' and is not named. In דניאל, מיכאל is called by name and is also described as 'one.' The shared word lets us carry the name מיכאל over to ישעיהו, and that is what supports רבי אלעזר בר אבינא's claim in step 29 that מיכאל arrives in a single flight.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from / it is learned from (the sign of a word-link between two פסוקים)
Learning from the same word that appears in two different פסוקים
A kind of angel described in ישעיהו
It is written here… and it is written there (the standard way of setting out a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is learned from 'one' and 'one.'
It is written here
"And one of the seraphim flew to me,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 6:6

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And behold, Michael, one of the chief ministers,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: the first ones, came to help me."
phrases.notes: דניאל 10:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we know the 'one' שרף is מיכאל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'אחד': דניאל calls מיכאל 'one,' so the 'one' in ישעיהו is מיכאל too.

steps.title: How many flights each angel needs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the flights: מיכאל in one, גבריאל in two, אליהו in four, the מלאך המות in eight, and in a time of plague the מלאך המות in one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: מיכאל arrives in one flight, גבריאל in two, אליהו in four, and the מלאך המות in eight. But in a time of plague, the מלאך המות arrives in one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that ranks the angels by how quickly they arrive. This closes the discussion of the angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds on step 29, where מיכאל needs one flight and גבריאל needs two, and adds אליהו and the מלאך המות to the list. The last line is an exception: during a plague the מלאך המות moves as fast as מיכאל.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (a ברייתא is being quoted)

steps.whatToRemember: Fewer flights means a faster angel. מיכאל is fastest (one flight), but in a plague the מלאך המות also arrives in one.
steps.confusionAlert: Fewer flights means faster, not slower. 'In one' is the quickest.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Michael, in one;
Gabriel, in two;
Elijah, in four;
and the Angel of Death, in eight.
phrases.notes: The word 'flights' is left out but meant on every line of this list.

phrases.english: And at a time of plague, in one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the one-flight and two-flight idea from step 29 into a full ranking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels are ranked by speed: מיכאל 1, גבריאל 2, אליהו 4, the מלאך המות 8, and the מלאך המות 1 during a plague.

steps.title: Say שמע again on your bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that even after saying קריאת שמע in shul at night, it is a מצוה to say it again in bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Even if a person already read קריאת שמע in the synagogue, it is a מצוה to read it on his bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of saying שמע at night. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the shul שמע does not take away the bedtime שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once he has said שמע at night in shul, he is finished. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that there is still a separate מצוה to say it right before going to sleep.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for קריאת שמע שעל המטה, the bedtime שמע said every night.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Even though a person read
the Shema in the synagogue,
it is a מצוה to read it upon his bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּרָא אָדָם קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the angel discussion and opens a new halachic topic about the night שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after the shul שמע at night, there is a מצוה to say שמע again on one's bed.

steps.title: A פסוק that hints to the bedtime שמע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings a פסוק from תהלים, 'say in your heart upon your bed and be still,' as a hint for saying שמע in bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: What is the פסוק for this? 'Tremble and do not sin; say in your heart upon your bed, and be still, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a פסוק to back up the rule of the bedtime שמע from step 33.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of saying something 'in your heart upon your bed' and then being still. That matches saying שמע in bed and then going quietly to sleep.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
What is the verse?
"Tremble, and do not sin;
say in your heart upon your bed,
and be still, Selah."
phrases.notes: תהלים 4:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק for רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה to say שמע on one's bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 4:5, 'אמרו בלבבכם על משכבכם ודמו סלה.'

steps.title: רב נחמן begins a comment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts to speak about רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. His words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב נחמן is about to comment on the bedtime שמע, and his words appear in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are here, so we do not yet know what רב נחמן will say. Keep the bedtime שמע rule from step 33 in mind, because that is what he is responding to.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from בבל who comments on the rule

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a comment on רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. The content continues in the next section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet; רב נחמן's words come next.
